cards.front: Centimetre (cm)
cards.back: A unit for measuring short lengths, such as a pencil.
cards.say: Centimetre. A unit for measuring short lengths, such as a pencil.

cards.front: Metre (m)
cards.back: A longer unit of length. 1 metre is 100 centimetres.
cards.say: Metre. A longer unit of length. One metre is one hundred centimetres.

cards.front: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
cards.say: How many centimetres are in one metre? One hundred centimetres.

cards.front: How many centimetres are in 2 metres?
cards.say: How many centimetres are in two metres? Two hundred centimetres.

cards.front: Half a metre is how many centimetres?
cards.say: Half a metre is how many centimetres? Fifty centimetres.

cards.front: Gram (g) and kilogram (kg)
cards.back: Units for mass. 1 kilogram is 1000 grams.
cards.say: Gram and kilogram. Units for mass. One kilogram is one thousand grams.

cards.front: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
cards.say: How many grams are in one kilogram? One thousand grams.

cards.front: Half a kilogram is how many grams?
cards.say: Half a kilogram is how many grams? Five hundred grams.

cards.front: Millilitre (ml) and litre (l)
cards.back: Units for capacity. 1 litre is 1000 millilitres.
cards.say: Millilitre and litre. Units for capacity. One litre is one thousand millilitres.

cards.front: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
cards.say: How many millilitres are in one litre? One thousand millilitres.

cards.front: Half a litre is how many millilitres?
cards.say: Half a litre is how many millilitres? Five hundred millilitres.

cards.front: Which unit would you use to measure a pencil: cm or m?
cards.say: Which unit would you use to measure a pencil: centimetres or metres? Centimetres. A pencil is short.

cards.front: Which unit would you use for the height of a door: cm or m?
cards.back: m. A door is about 2 metres tall.
cards.say: Which unit would you use for the height of a door: centimetres or metres? Metres. A door is about two metres tall.

cards.front: Which unit would you use for a bag of rice: g or kg?
cards.say: Which unit would you use for a bag of rice: grams or kilograms? Kilograms.

cards.front: Which unit would you use for a spoon of salt: g or kg?
cards.say: Which unit would you use for a spoon of salt: grams or kilograms? Grams.

cards.front: Which unit would you use for a cup of juice: ml or l?
cards.say: Which unit would you use for a cup of juice: millilitres or litres? Millilitres.

cards.front: Which unit would you use for water in a bucket: ml or l?
cards.back: l. A bucket holds many litres.
cards.say: Which unit would you use for water in a bucket: millilitres or litres? Litres. A bucket holds many litres.

cards.front: Which is longer: 1 m or 90 cm?
cards.back: 1 m. 1 m is 100 cm and 100 is more than 90.
cards.say: Which is longer: one metre or ninety centimetres? One metre. One metre is one hundred centimetres and one hundred is more than ninety.

cards.front: Which is heavier: 1 kg or 900 g?
cards.say: Which is heavier: one kilogram or nine hundred grams? One kilogram. One kilogram is one thousand grams.

cards.front: Which holds more: 1 l or 800 ml?
cards.say: Which holds more: one litre or eight hundred millilitres? One litre. One litre is one thousand millilitres.

cards.front: Thermometer
cards.back: A tool for measuring temperature. We read it in degrees Celsius, written °C.
cards.say: Thermometer. A tool for measuring temperature. We read it in degrees Celsius.

cards.front: Water freezes at what temperature?
cards.say: Water freezes at what temperature? Zero degrees Celsius.

cards.front: Water boils at what temperature?
cards.say: Water boils at what temperature? One hundred degrees Celsius.

cards.front: Which is hotter: 30 °C or 10 °C?
cards.say: Which is hotter: thirty degrees Celsius or ten degrees Celsius? Thirty degrees Celsius.

cards.front: A ribbon is 40 cm. Another is 25 cm. How much longer is the first?
cards.say: A ribbon is forty centimetres. Another is twenty-five centimetres. How much longer is the first? Fifteen centimetres. Forty take away twenty-five is fifteen.
